method: Read the exact cutoff-version primary source, including the abstract, contribution/conclusion and explicit future-work/open-question passages, before any post-cutoff search. Eligibility requires a source-grounded open direction plus an object, comparator or property, measurable endpoint and falsification condition that can be frozen without later results.

rows.source_locator: PDF pp. 1-4 abstract/introduction and survey challenge taxonomy
rows.source_basis: The source is a survey collecting challenges from advanced application domains. The inspected cutoff text does not leave one uniquely defined unresolved proposition with a fixed object, comparator and falsification gate. Turning one of the survey topics into such a question would be a reviewer-created question rather than a source-only lock.

rows.source_locator: PDF pp. 1-3 abstract/introduction; pp. 10-12 discussion and future-work passages
rows.source_basis: The source studies three commercial smart toys and identifies privacy-policy and network-security mismatches. It explicitly motivates auditing more toys and automating the mapping from vague privacy policies to verifiable technical properties. The object and endpoint can be frozen as policy-to-observable-property agreement and independently reproduced violation detection, without using later findings.
rows.candidate_question: Across a preregistered sample of connected children's toys, can an automated policy-to-property audit recover the same objectively verifiable privacy and network-security violations as independent manual analysis while reducing analyst effort without increasing false negatives?
rows.comparison_and_metric: automated policy-to-property audit versus independently blinded manual audit on the same toy firmware/network traces; violation recall, false-positive rate and analyst time
rows.falsification_gate: The automation fails if recall is materially lower than the manual audit, false positives increase beyond a predeclared margin, or analyst-time savings disappear after review of ambiguous policy language. A larger vulnerability count alone is not a success label.

rows.source_locator: PDF pp. 1-2 abstract/introduction; pp. 9-10 conclusion and future-work discussion
rows.source_basis: The paper presents a Six Sigma-inspired catalog mapping Industry 4.0 requirements to security controls and implementation-cost estimates. Its future directions concern adapting the catalog to scenarios and standards and automating assessment, but the inspected source does not define one fixed comparative endpoint or falsification condition. A later benchmark would be an externally invented question.

rows.source_locator: PDF pp. 2-3 open challenge; pp. 21-22 discussion of richer behavior and whitelist convergence
rows.source_basis: SERENIoT explicitly states that correct whitelisted IoT behavior is open, and asks whether a collaborative intrusion-detection system can converge on permitted connections when richer device behavior and adversarial observations are present. The source supplies an observable policy set, convergence behavior and security/performance tradeoffs.
rows.candidate_question: For heterogeneous smart-home devices with software-update and adversarial-traffic regimes, can collaborative whitelist learning converge to a stable permitted-connection set while keeping false blocking and attacker-injected allowance below predeclared thresholds?
rows.comparison_and_metric: collaborative majority-derived whitelist versus a fixed manufacturer/local-observation baseline across benign, update and adversarial traces; convergence time, false-block rate, attacker-allowance rate and policy size
rows.falsification_gate: The claim fails if convergence is absent within the predeclared horizon, or if either false blocking or attacker allowance exceeds the fixed safety margin relative to the baseline. A proof-of-concept throughput result alone does not settle policy correctness.

rows.source_locator: PDF pp. 1-3 contribution/evaluation; p. 10 conclusion and explicit plan to add constraint handling through a solver
rows.source_basis: The source presents an Avocado combinatorial-interaction-testing framework and explicitly plans constraint handling through a constraint solver. The source leaves an implementation-and-evaluation question that can be frozen as constrained versus unconstrained test generation on invalid-configuration detection and execution cost.
rows.candidate_question: On constrained virtual-machine configuration spaces, does adding solver-backed constraint handling to Avocado reduce invalid or redundant test executions while preserving or improving detection of invalid configurations relative to unconstrained t-way generation?
rows.comparison_and_metric: solver-backed constrained CIT versus the source's unconstrained t-way generation on the same configuration model; invalid-configuration detection recall, executed-test count, invalid-test rate and wall-clock cost
rows.falsification_gate: No reduction in invalid/redundant executions at non-inferior detection recall, or a benefit that disappears on held-out configuration models, falsifies the claimed practical value. A framework implementation without a matched comparison is partial progress only.

rows.source_locator: PDF pp. 1-3 method and evaluation; pp. 16-17 conclusion/future work on missing UML sequence diagrams and broader applications
rows.source_basis: The source evaluates security-pattern selection and LTL checking on ten Web applications, then explicitly identifies two unresolved limitations: broader application types and patterns without UML sequence diagrams. This supports a source-only generalization question with objective trace-property detection outcomes.
rows.candidate_question: Can the security-pattern checking approach generalize from UML-sequence-diagram-supported Web applications to applications or patterns lacking those diagrams by using code annotations, while preserving independently verified behavioral-property detection precision and recall?
rows.comparison_and_metric: original UML-sequence-diagram pipeline versus the proposed annotation-based representation on project-disjoint applications/patterns; property-detection precision, recall, annotation effort and runtime
rows.falsification_gate: The generalization fails if precision or recall falls beyond a predeclared margin, annotations cannot be independently checked, or the apparent result depends on the same projects used to design the representation. More application examples without a matched representation comparison are not decisive.

limitation: These are targeted source-section decisions, not exhaustive page-by-page annotation. Four eligible questions now require bounded future checks; no later result was used to decide eligibility, and no direct resolution label is implied.
